content:
Sean Gallagher: starting a thread to lock game day scenarios for Dedicated burst (overload + mitigations). we need owners + timeline so we can get a calendar hold out.

Sean Gallagher: ask: please propose (a) 1-2 scenarios you want to run, (b) what “success” means, (c) what knobs/mitigations we’ll exercise (caps, cooldown, circuit breaker, routing fallback), and (d) any prereqs.

Rafael Mendes: :eyes: yep. we should run this before we turn on the GA rollout gate in more regions. i’d like to target week of Feb 17 if we can.

Allison Grant: +1. prereq from obs side: dashboards/alerts wired in staging and at least one canary tenant in prod (internal) so we can validate label cardinality + alert noise.

Peter Holtz: for routing/SRE i’d like a scenario where admission controller goes “soft unavailable” (timeouts) and we confirm routing behavior is deterministic + safe (no thundering herd / no cross-tenant leakage). mitigation should be fallback-to-baseline + backpressure.

Keiko Yamamoto: from guardrails: we should simulate burst pool saturation + neighbor impact. i want to see the global fleet safety cap trip + the “reduce burst ratio automatically” path, and confirm cooldown prevents oscillation.

Talia Benson: tracking. can someone drop proposed scenario list + owners here and i’ll translate to the game day doc + calendar invite.

Sean Gallagher: ok, draft list. pls poke holes.

Sean Gallagher: Scenario A (Pool saturation / fairness under load)
- Setup: 3 tenants on same region/hw class burst pool. Tenant1 bursts aggressively, Tenant2 bursts moderately, Tenant3 non-burst baseline only.
- Inject: drive pool to >90% utilization with Tenant1, plus occasional telemetry lag (~30-60s) so the controller is making decisions on stale-ish signals.
- Expected: fairness enforcement prevents starvation; Tenant1 gets denials w/ reason codes, Tenant2 continues to get some burst, Tenant3 latency p95 doesn’t regress beyond allowed delta.
- Mitigation steps to exercise: lower per-tenant cap, increase cooldown window, enable global circuit breaker if neighbor impact crosses threshold.

Sean Gallagher: Scenario B (Admission controller degraded)
- Setup: routing calls admission controller inline.
- Inject: 20% timeouts + 5xx from admission controller for 10 min.
- Expected: routing doesn’t retry in a tight loop; uses cached decision TTL OR defaults to “deny burst / serve baseline” (whatever is spec’d), and we preserve determinism (same request id => same behavior).
- Mitigation steps: flip feature flag to bypass controller; verify kill switch disables burst for pool.

Sean Gallagher: Scenario C (SLO regression gate)
- Setup: enable burst for internal tenant in staging/prod-canary.
- Inject: increase tail latency for non-burst tenant via synthetic load (or force queue depth) such that p95 delta > threshold.
- Expected: SLO gate reduces/halts burst automatically + pages appropriately (or alerts only, depending on policy).

Rafael Mendes: scenario A/B/C all good. we probably can’t do all 3 in one 60min block. propose: A + B in main session, C as “pre/post” validation using load test harness + alerting.

Vanessa Ortiz: on A: we should explicitly validate that non-burst tenant sees stable throughput. latency-only is insufficient; also watch queue depth + “admitted_burst_gpu_seconds” by tenant.

Allison Grant: on C: we need crisp metric definition for “neighbor impact” that we can actually trigger reliably. otherwise it’s flaky.

Allison Grant: suggestion: use an explicit synthetic SLO guardrail metric from the routing tier: `nonburst_p95_latency_delta_ms` computed vs 30m baseline, and trip when > X for Y minutes. then we can force it by pushing a controlled overload (queue depth) and watch the gate action.

Peter Holtz: +1 on having a metric we can deterministically trigger. if we rely on “real” p95 we’ll fight traffic randomness.

Keiko Yamamoto: for A, can we test both “immediate deny” and “queue/backpressure”? (depending on config). i want to see behavior when we choose to queue up to N seconds vs return 429.

Sean Gallagher: yep. i think spec says: when burst denied due to cap/fairness => immediate deny with reason; when pool overloaded => 429 with `overload` reason + `retry_after_ms`? (someone confirm). we should test both response shapes.

Mina Haddad: (looping in from routing side) spec as implemented right now: routing gets `ADMIT_BASELINE_ONLY` vs `ADMIT_BURST` vs `DENY_OVERLOAD` from controller. for `DENY_OVERLOAD` we do client-visible 429 w/ `x-redwood-retry-after-ms` header and we do NOT attempt cross-region. for baseline-only we route to dedicated baseline path.

Mina Haddad: so A should cover baseline-only and overload. B covers controller timeout -> we currently default to baseline-only after 100ms timeout. (peter/elana added a guard so we don’t pile up).

Sergio Costa: for prereqs: dashboards are in Grafana folder “Dedicated Burst / Pools”. i still need sign-off on alert thresholds to avoid paging during game day :)

Rafael Mendes: we can run game day with paging suppressed (alerts visible but no pager) as long as we document it and run a “real” paging test later.

Sean Gallagher: i’m ok with that. but for SLO gate we should see the automation fire (even if no pager). otherwise it’s not meaningful.

Talia Benson: timeline check: can we do Thurs Feb 20 10:00-11:30 PT? (gives time for Sergio to finish dashboards and Keiko to prep load)

Keiko Yamamoto: works for me. i need by Feb 18: final cap values + ability to toggle telemetry smoothing on/off in staging.

Allison Grant: i can commit to having dashboards + alert rules in staging by Feb 19 EOD. will share a “game day view” link.

Peter Holtz: i’ll own B scenario execution (controller timeout + kill switch). need someone from platform to run the fault injection (timeouts/5xx). if nobody, i can do via envoy fault filter in staging.

Sean Gallagher: let’s assign owners:
- Scenario A owner: Keiko (guardrails) + Vanessa (fleet signals) + Sean (facilitation)
- Scenario B owner: Peter (routing) + Mina (routing) + (platform volunteer?)
- Scenario C owner: Allison (metrics/alerts) + Sean (SLO gate verification)

Mina Haddad: i can coordinate w/ Ethan’s team for the platform piece. if they can’t join live, we’ll do envoy fault injection.

Vanessa Ortiz: for A i’ll prep a “pool saturation checklist”: what telemetry panels to watch, and what the “safe abort” criteria are (if we see non-burst degrade > threshold we stop).

Rafael Mendes: also: let’s make sure we exercise the runbook steps. game day isn’t just “watch it happen”; we should practice mitigation:
1) reduce per-tenant burst cap
2) reduce pool max burst ratio
3) flip global circuit breaker
4) disable burst via kill switch
5) comms template to Support/CS (even internal)

Sean Gallagher: +1. i’ll put those as explicit tasks in the agenda.

Sergio Costa: quick question: do we want to validate denial reason code breakdown panel? i can add a table by tenant + reason if useful.

Allison Grant: yes please. but keep labels controlled: tenant_id as hashed/short id, not customer name.

Sergio Costa: ack. i’ll use `tenant_slug` for internal only and `tenant_hash` everywhere else.

Talia Benson: action items i’m capturing:
- Sean: finalize scenario doc + agenda (by Feb 14)
- Keiko/Vanessa: load profiles + abort criteria (by Feb 18)
- Allison/Sergio: dashboards + alert rules in staging (by Feb 19)
- Peter/Mina: fault injection plan for controller timeouts + kill switch verification (by Feb 18)
- Rafael: confirm paging suppression approach + how we’ll record outcomes (by Feb 17)

Rafael Mendes: add: we need a note taker + a single place to file follow-ups (Linear tickets). i can do note taker if needed.

Sean Gallagher: i’ll do facilitation, rafael note taker works.

Mina Haddad: what environment? staging is best for fault injection, but we should also validate at least one “prod canary” guardrail works (without injecting chaos). maybe a tiny burst with internal tenant.

Sean Gallagher: agree. game day primary in staging. optional 15-min “prod canary check” after: verify denial codes + metering counters increment + no alert noise.

Keiko Yamamoto: ok but for prod canary we should keep it below 20% of pool safety cap.

Vanessa Ortiz: yep. also confirm circuit breaker is armed but not tripped.

Allison Grant: last prereq: someone confirm we have the debug endpoint enabled for “why was i denied” (redacted). otherwise we’ll struggle to explain denials during game day.

Peter Holtz: it’s behind internal auth in staging. i’ll verify it’s reachable and add to the agenda.

Sean Gallagher: cool. thanks all. talia pls send calendar hold once you draft.

Talia Benson: will do. i’ll send invite w/ agenda + links once sean drops doc link.

Rafael Mendes: :thumbsup: let’s make sure we timebox the chaos so we don’t accidentally soak staging all day.

Sean Gallagher: lol yes. hard stop at 90 min.
